notes: NovaShell 152 fixes saved-theme boot consistency and gives every shared Retro window one clear close control.
changes: A saved Ultra Retro preference now survives the visual migration on first launch instead of being reset to a modern theme; embedded Workflow Proof also inherits the selected theme immediately.
Shared Retro window chrome now adopts nested legacy close icons into its title bar and removes duplicate × controls, including Pokédex detail sheets.
Workflow Proof now explains its local-only checklist purpose in plain language: repeat a launch, backup, install, or handoff without losing steps or sending data anywhere.

Second Brain now records a source-adoption audit and updated migration map: reviewed focus, inventory, audio, weather, transit, dashboard, Brain, world, and FTP plugin patterns are represented by clean NovaShell surfaces; unresolved higher-risk candidates remain explicitly held back.
Second Brain search now calls the existing local knowledge index after a short debounce, so content-only terms work in both the reader list and Structure map without an external provider.
The new source-module smoke script validates every removable app manifest, declared local entry, JavaScript syntax, and local HTTP response without reading private local data.

Second Brain now has a Structure map that projects the same indexed local Markdown folders and categories as interactive nodes. Selecting a node opens that exact indexed note; the map does not invent semantic relationships.

Signal Board now summarizes workflow states including planned, active, completed, failed, and needs review, and visually flags entries that need attention. Its full modular asset set is now part of the offline shell cache.

Owner-authored Second Brain notes can now be removed from an in-app confirmation window. The route only resolves notes inside the dedicated ignored owner-note folder and requires REMOVE OWNER NOTE; imported and built-in notes remain read-only.
A persisted workflow whose in-memory runner disappears after a local helper restart now becomes needs review instead of being left falsely running or silently marked complete.

Second Brain can now save an owner-authored local Markdown note under ignored local storage after validating its title, category, and bounded body. The note is indexed for Relay context but grants no file, shell, network, or edit power.

Signal Board is a new removable, read-only local dashboard for Relay knowledge, modular apps, durable workflows, and Project Board activity. It uses existing local NovaShell endpoints and makes no model or network call.
Second Brain now has focused filters for decisions, workflows, boundaries, maps, guides, and optional local imports, alongside its local full-text reader.

Relay now carries a clean capability portfolio, source-informed build decision, workflow playbook, and reviewable next-integration candidates. These are NovaShell-authored summaries; no private archive or FTP content is bundled.
Relay workflow proof created a removable local Workflow Proof app, made a constrained harness core change, and recorded a separate reviewed external-workspace handoff.
Workflow cards now reconcile a completed Local Codex job into the durable local ledger instead of remaining stale after normal polling.
Second Brain is now a full NovaShell page with searchable local notes, categories, readable source previews, and a live harness summary.

Relay now has a persistent Long Work panel for modular project workflows and external/API handoffs. Only reviewed project workflows can enter the fixed NovaShell coding runner after typed confirmation; external handoffs are never auto-executed.
Retro Dark is a persistent charcoal-and-phosphor theme that keeps NovaShell’s retro material and high contrast without using a flat black overlay.
Relay now shows a dedicated Second Brain browser launcher with the local indexed-note/import count and a clear read-only boundary.
Pokédex now resolves card artwork by the Pokémon API identifier, including forms such as Galarian Mr. Mime, with official-art/home/sprite fallbacks.
Pokédex detail sheets now show flavor text, base stats, notable moves, abilities, and weaknesses in a high-contrast Retro layout.
Offline Operator can now offer an explicit Steam Link launch; NovaShell only hands ChromeOS the launch request and never reads Steam account data.
Settings now lists removable Relay-created desktop utilities with an in-app typed removal confirmation. These are isolated in user-apps/ and never remove NovaShell core files.
Relay Action Ledger now accepts owner comments, and guarded core rollbacks write their confirmation/result pair into the same ignored local history.

Relay's Offline Operator is a real local-only action layer: it can inspect safe system, owned-game, modular-app, and Project Board metadata or open selected NovaShell screens without a provider key, model, network request, shell command, file-content read, or write.
Every Offline Operator result now shows its small tool trace and data boundary, so its actions are visible instead of implied.
Local Codex no longer requires a Relay cloud-provider profile. It remains explicitly confirmed, locked to the NovaShell checkout, and separate from optional provider keys.

Relay's provider page now labels external routes honestly: provider access is optional, no automatic request is made after saving, and free-tier availability/privacy are controlled by each external provider.
Settings now includes a saved Soft Reminder. Start it at the default 4½-minute interval or choose another interval; a gentle two-note chime continues through NovaShell navigation until stopped.
Social Desk is a removable local app for public Bluesky profiles and topic searches. It is read-only, needs no account, and keeps only the shortcuts you choose on this device.

Recovery Station now works inside NovaShell World: log water or a recovery break directly into your existing browser-local Reset Station data, with the full Reset Station available as an optional surface.

NovaShell World now also has an in-world saved Writer note, live Oak Park weather readout, Browse quick launchpad, Relay local status, and a positional Orbit speaker; their full apps remain optional second actions.

NovaShell World has usable in-world Library, Project Board, and Settings desks: inspect library names, read live task counts/latest work, and change themes without leaving the building; full NovaShell surfaces remain optional.
Space/A now toggles an open station panel closed, and walking away from a station closes its panel automatically.
NovaShell World now shows one small, readable bottom control dock that automatically changes from WASD/arrow instructions to Xbox left-stick, A, and B instructions when a controller is present.
NovaShell World reacquires keyboard focus after a tap, window focus, or return to the tab. Escape/B now closes a station panel, while Shift/RT is the optional faster walk modifier.

The World has broad physical doorways between its four rooms; a movement-path check now reaches every room directly from spawn instead of trapping right-side destinations behind a long central collision wall.
Every local user-app launch now includes an automatic folder revision, so updated HTML, styles, and modules receive a fresh launch URL instead of reusing a stale PWA or iframe response.
NovaShell World now has no header, room status, proximity prompt, or renderer-made floating text at all; those elements were removed from the markup and renderer rather than merely hidden.
NovaShell World's intentional interaction panel now uses explicit high-contrast text in every theme, including Ultra Retro.
Maker Desk is now NovaShell World's real local setup editor: choose room finishes and up to eight owned-game arcade cabinets, save locally, then enter the building with that setup applied.
NovaShell World no longer keeps developer-style labels, prompts, or a status HUD on top of the building; only an intentional station interaction opens a readable panel.
NovaShell World keeps filtered 3D labels out of the way, moves station names into readable interaction panels, and makes Orbit and every external surface an explicit optional choice.
NovaShell World now has a low-key positional room tone that grows and pans as you approach the Orbit speaker after a user interaction enables sound.
Theme changes now synchronize through settings, the desktop, open panels, and Orbit even when the setting changes in a separate same-origin window.

GBA multiplayer now describes mGBA's real link flow honestly: NovaShell opens the first game and mGBA's New Multiplayer Window creates the link, rather than pretending two unrelated CLI windows are linked.
NovaShell World now takes WASD and arrow-key input through both code and key fallbacks, focuses its canvas on launch, prevents page-scroll key loss, and uses larger high-contrast labels.
Pocket Archive and all eleven bundled local apps received a clean runtime and interaction smoke pass; a real GBA game now reaches a live EmulatorJS canvas again.

If Chrome displays a cached NovaShell shell while the local helper is stopped, the desktop now explains exactly why games, apps, files, and local tools cannot work and provides the one-line restart command.
The normal Chromebook launcher now opens the correct 127.0.0.1 NovaShell address with a cache-busting launch URL.
Selective restore now previews new files, conflicts, preserved entries, blocked archive entries, exact group samples, and replacement safety copies before extracting anything.
A changed backup or destination invalidates the reviewed restore fingerprint, so it must be inspected again before a write occurs.
Every shared Retro window now has one consistent draggable title bar and a larger touch-safe close target instead of overlapping duplicate close controls.
Every built-in NovaShell app now inherits one centered, touch-sized Back control, including apps that previously had a mismatched link or no Back control.
Orbit's compact player now recovers unsupported and stale visual states instead of occasionally showing a blank canvas.
The top-left signal beacon now uses matching loop endpoints for fluid motion without a visible restart seam.
Retro Settings adds sixteen original CSS-only mixed-color pattern wallpapers that remain fast and offline.
Relay's Second Brain, provider routes, guarded core workspace, Web Component app workshop, and local action history now load together as one visible harness.
Generated apps use a review-only sandbox preview, an explicit CREATE APP confirmation, a four-file module layout, and a local plan-preview-confirm-result ledger.
N64 versus launch now confirms Chrome sees two distinct controllers before starting and clearly shows whether player two is ready.
Storage details now include a read-only cleanup and recovery coach for stale Downloads, recoverable Trash, and the last completed selective backup.
Backup completion state is stored only in ignored local data and never includes credentials or file contents.
Hosted NovaShell now includes Retro/Cobalt, touch/controller navigation, explicit IndexedDB game selection, Orbit, Notes, Kanban, Weather, Browse, Relay guidance, and browser backup.
Public docs and the parity matrix now identify exactly which hosted features work and which still require local NovaShell.
Show large files, open my music folder, and back up game saves now resolve to explicit NovaShell routes instead of falling through as unknown text.
Sensitive-looking intents show a controller-compatible preview stating what data is read and confirming that no file or backup changes happen automatically.
The import screen now has one transaction owner and sends the required catalog key and source path after a local ROM copy.
Existing owned games update their private card without overwriting existing artwork, and interrupted metadata appears in the review queue rather than vanishing.
Manage local games now has All, Needs details, and Multiplayer queues plus search, location identity, a consistent editor window, and owner-art replacement with ignored local backups.
Weather Station now uses one self-contained modular runtime instead of layered legacy scripts and styles.
Forecast URLs can specify a place, public captures skip private local defaults, and the last successful report remains usable when weather sources are offline.
Xbox pads are sorted by physical browser index and assigned independently to player one through player four, including controllers exposed after the emulator starts.
N64 fighter detection now includes Mortal Kombat, Killer Instinct, ClayFighter, Fighter's Destiny, Mace, War Gods, Dark Rift, and other local-versus titles.
The full EmulatorJS map now includes both analog sticks, triggers, D-pad, face buttons, shoulders, and stick clicks.
N64 games marked multiplayer—and known local-versus classics—show a direct two-player launch in their game sheet.
Rail Finder now has a private-key CTA departure and arrival board, and Reset Station has expanded breathing and recovery routines.
NovaShell World now uses a low-resolution multi-room pixel building with real local stations.
